boundary: Author-written definition checks, not human validation, reader measurements, or ratification evidence. No case licenses an external action.

cases.scenario: The full population is A and B. The message names A, B, among-others.
cases.expected: The marker does not claim completeness and does not assert that a third member exists. It can be true when the named list happens to be complete.
cases.forbidden_inference: There must be an unlisted member; therefore the reported set is a proper subset.

cases.scenario: The message says the scoped allowlist admits A, B, and-no-others.
cases.expected: It claims completeness of that allowlist at the stated kind and scope, not completeness of every list in the document.
cases.forbidden_inference: Every other named set in the report is also complete.

cases.scenario: A sample S is explicitly a proper subset of the population. The message completely lists the failures inside S with and-no-others.
cases.expected: The enumeration can be complete within the sample while the sample is not the whole population.
cases.forbidden_inference: No failures exist in the unobserved population.

cases.scenario: An export claims support for csv, parquet, among-others. YAML support is not otherwise stated.
cases.expected: The marker neither admits nor excludes YAML and does not decide whether it belongs to the named format kind.
cases.forbidden_inference: YAML is accepted simply because the list is open.

cases.scenario: S is a complete population of four tests. Exactly one failed. The report says whole(S): some-but-not-all tests failed.
cases.expected: Complete population coverage and a proper nonempty set of failures are compatible; at least one test passed.
cases.forbidden_inference: The report covers only part of the test population.

cases.scenario: S is a proper sample of four tests and all four failed. The report says part(S): some-or-all sampled tests failed.
cases.expected: The quantifier is true within S and leaves its all-case open. No result for unsampled tests follows.
cases.forbidden_inference: Some unsampled test passed, or all population members failed.

cases.scenario: S is the whole population and all members satisfy P. The report says some-or-all members satisfy P.
cases.expected: The clause is true but less informative than an all claim; it does not assert speaker ignorance.
cases.forbidden_inference: The author cannot have counted every member.

cases.scenario: S is a proper sample and none of its members satisfies P. Either some-or-all or some-but-not-all is asserted over S.
cases.expected: Both assertions are false because both require at least one satisfying member; partial coverage does not remove that lower bound.
cases.forbidden_inference: An unseen satisfying member makes the assertion about S true.

cases.scenario: Assign exactly one reviewer to each of reports A, B and C, may-vary-across(reports). Ada is eligible and has capacity for all three.
cases.expected: Ada/Ada/Ada is permitted. Permission to vary is not a requirement for different reviewers.
cases.forbidden_inference: Three different reviewers are required.

cases.scenario: Three reports must have the same reviewer. That reviewer later conducts one separate review per report.
cases.expected: A shared reviewer choice is compatible with three separate review acts; cross-member equality does not make the work one collective act.
cases.forbidden_inference: same-for-all means one joint review instead of three.

cases.scenario: Three agents verify one checkpoint as-one and wear different approved uniform colours.
cases.expected: The verification is one group act. It supplies no equality rule for a separate colour-choice slot.
cases.forbidden_inference: Acting as-one forces all choices or properties of participants to be equal.

cases.scenario: The choice set is a singleton, or alternatively is empty.
cases.expected: The singleton is in scope and the equality distinction has no effect. The empty set is outside the shared-choice construction; do not infer a vacuous permission.
cases.forbidden_inference: The qualifier itself supplies missing members or a missing one-choice-per-member requirement.

cases.scenario: An action says extra-retries(2), no-retry.
cases.expected: The numeric limit does not override the repeatability warning or authorize a blind repeat. Resolve the conflict before acting.
cases.forbidden_inference: A positive retry budget makes repetition safe.

cases.scenario: An action says total-attempts(1), idempotent.
cases.expected: The count permits at most one execution in scope. Safe repeatability does not expand the stated budget.
cases.forbidden_inference: Idempotent means an unlimited number of attempts is authorized.

cases.scenario: An action is marked no-retry and the response was lost after possible execution.
cases.expected: Completion is uncertain; verification or escalation comes before deciding what to do next.
cases.forbidden_inference: No response proves no action occurred, so retry blindly.

cases.scenario: One instruction permits extra-retries(2); another permits total-attempts(2). Both actions are otherwise authorized and repeatable.
cases.expected: Their maximum execution counts are three and two respectively. These are ceilings, not instructions to perform unnecessary retries.
cases.forbidden_inference: The two numeral-2 forms permit the same total, or require every allowed attempt.

cases.scenario: The current quantity is 10. Compare set-to(3) with adjust-by(+3).
cases.expected: The requested destinations are 3 and 13 respectively, assuming consistent units and no intervening update.
cases.forbidden_inference: Both forms name a final value of 3.

cases.scenario: The earlier quantity is unknown. Compare set-to(30) with adjust-by(+30).
cases.expected: The first names a destination of 30; the second's final value remains unknown.
cases.forbidden_inference: Use zero as the unknown starting value.

cases.scenario: Starting at 10, apply two explicitly ordered set-to(3) updates, or instead two explicitly ordered adjust-by(+3) updates.
cases.expected: The final numeric values are 3 and 16. This arithmetic says nothing about duplicate notifications, billing or other side effects.
cases.forbidden_inference: An assignment-looking update proves the whole external operation is idempotent.

cases.scenario: A rate is 10 percent. The instruction says adjust-by(+3 percentage points); another update is concurrent and unordered.
cases.expected: The isolated first update requests 13 percent. The qualifier alone does not order the concurrent updates or make storage atomic.
cases.forbidden_inference: Read the change as a 3 percent relative increase, or infer a concurrency order.

cases.scenario: P offers option X with proposal-by(P). P also states a personal will-as-plan to prepare supporting work.
cases.expected: An offered option and a revisable personal plan do not establish an authoritative selection of X.
cases.forbidden_inference: A plan upgrades a proposal to a decision.

cases.scenario: A clause marks an option decision-by(A).
cases.expected: It claims a selection by A in A's relevant standing. It does not independently prove that standing, execution, or permission for the recipient to act.
cases.forbidden_inference: A decision label is proof of authorization and successful execution.

cases.scenario: A speaker says will-as-promise to deliver a report, with no statement about the group's choice of a deployment option.
cases.expected: The promise concerns the speaker's undertaking; no group decision about the deployment option follows.
cases.forbidden_inference: A commitment by one person makes a decision for the group.

cases.scenario: A forecast predicts that an offered option will be selected tomorrow.
cases.expected: A prediction of a future choice is neither a present authoritative decision nor an undertaking to cause that choice.
cases.forbidden_inference: A confident forecast grants present permission to implement the option.
